links.note: Nasal hair and mucus filter inhaled air, cartilage rings keep the trachea open - both are air-passage features of the human respiratory system (161).

What is seen in a leaf-peel mount under low and high power: epidermal cells, the stoma, and two bean-shaped guard cells with chloroplasts - guard-cell structure (154). The sibling technique items (staining, blotting) test no concept and are left out.
Two parasites plus how fungi feed (saprotrophically) - both branches of heterotrophic nutrition (155), not autotrophic (152).

Cramps come from lactic acid built up by anaerobic breakdown of glucose when oxygen runs short - the anaerobic arm of the respiration pathways (159). Not 161: the item is about the pathway, not about breathing.
After losing length of small intestine the bear should eat meat, because a plant diet needs a longer canal - alimentary-canal length versus diet (156).
Why diffusion is insufficient in large animals and what arrangement replaces it - the life-processes argument for organ systems (151).

Functions of bile - neutralising chyme, giving the alkaline medium pancreatic enzymes need, and emulsifying fat for lipase - is enzyme-support chemistry (157). The pancreas endocrine/exocrine half has no concept in this chapter.
180 L of filtrate against 1.5 L of urine: selective reabsorption along the nephron (168).
Bread turns sweet because salivary amylase makes maltose; part (b) turns on the absence of cellulase in humans - both are enzyme facts (157), not organ anatomy (156).
Why diffusion suffices for a single cell but not for a multicellular body - the life-processes definition and its consequence (151).
Three of the four parts are respiratory - tracheal cartilage, alveolar sac, larynx (161). The chlorophyll part is a one-word aside on 153 and does not carry the item.
Defines excretion and asks two vital kidney functions, including osmoregulation (168).
Urea, nephron, and ADH regulation of urine volume - three facts all inside the excretory system concept (168).
Part (a), the substantive part, is villi and why they matter for absorption (156). Part (b) on residual lung volume is a single aside on 161.

How water rises in a tall tree with no pump: transpiration creates suction/negative pressure in the xylem - that is 167 specifically. The xylem-versus-phloem comparison in part (b) is 166, but the item leads on the pull.

Site of gaseous exchange - a respiratory-system structure item (161). KEY DEFECT: the marked answer is 'Alveoli and throat'; exchange happens at the alveoli and the capillaries surrounding them, option D.
Exhaled air turns lime water milky because respiration releases CO2 - the product of the aerobic pathway (159). 161 would be the plumbing, not what the test demonstrates.
Amoeba digests food in a food vacuole - holozoic heterotrophic nutrition (155), not the human digestive system (156).
Without salivary amylase, starch-to-sugar breakdown fails - a direct enzyme-substrate item (157).
The anal sphincter regulates exit of unabsorbed food - the terminal organ of the alimentary canal (156). 158 is the propulsive movement, not the sphincter's regulating role.
Three pairs of salivary glands - digestive-organ anatomy (156). The enzyme they secrete would be 157; the count is not an enzyme fact.
Villi serve absorption of digested food, not emulsification or breakdown - the distractors are all enzyme roles, so the item tests the absorptive design of the intestine (156).
Xylem carries water and minerals from root to shoot (166).
Transplanting a young plant reduces root surface area, so uptake into the xylem falls (166). Not 167: nothing about the transpiration pull changes.

Matches each excretory step to its structure - glomerulus, collecting duct, ureter, bladder (168). KEY DEFECT: the marked 'incorrect' pair is Concentration of urine-Collecting duct, which is in fact a correct pairing; all four options as printed are correct, so the item has no defensible answer.
Two of the three true statements and the answer's whole point are about removing nitrogenous waste in the kidney and the purpose of urine (168). The CO2 clause is incidental.
